_meta: Original curation, not derived from content/grammar_data.py (the scraped-from-jlptsensei.com file — see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and the JLPT mock-exam plan for why). There is no official JLPT grammar list published by JEES/the Japan Foundation; every study site's list is its own independent observation of patterns that recur on real papers, which is why they overlap heavily without copying one another. This file is that same kind of independent curation, cross-checked against multiple such sources during construction rather than lifted from any one of them, holding only the grammar-point identity (pattern name, its attachment structure, a short original gloss, and its conventional level) -- the facts about which patterns exist and roughly where they're taught, not any site's explanations or example sentences. Used by study/exam_grammar_gen.py as the checklist a per-item LLM call generates ORIGINAL example sentences and distractors from; the meaning/structure fields here are deliberately short (a one-line gloss, not an explanation) to stay clearly on the facts side of the line.
